findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed 2 containers of meat purée to be hot holding at a temperature of 110F. Discussed with PIC, meats were then transferred to stovetop and reheated. Ensure any TCS food being hot held are kept above 135F at all times. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of thickened water and apple juice to held past their 7 day date marking threshold. Discussed with PIC, thickened water and apple juice were discarded. Ensure staff is checking date marking on TCS foods. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the middle container holding sugar and flour to be soiled with food accumulation. Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents contamination. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the reach-in cooler across from the hot holding steam table to have a broken gasket/seal. The gasket should be flush and connected to the door to properly seal the cooler. Temperature issues could arise from a broken gasket/seal. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the gasket/seal is replaced by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager present during the inspection. Staff working the lunch hour were all food handler’s per staff members. Ensure more than 1 CFPM is available at the facility. Facility should have at least 2-3 CFPM’s to cover all operational hours (breakfast, lunch, and dinner). Discussed with staff. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sani bucket to be 0 ppm. Staff indicated it had not been changed out since breakfast. Ensure sani buckets are frequently changed in order to keep concentration at appropriate levels to properly sanitize. Facility is utilizing quaternary ammonium in sani buckets. Quat should be 200-400 ppm. Discussed with staff. Employee re-made the sani bucket per the Inspector’s request - 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the milk chest cooler to have a layer of spilled milk at the bottom of the cooler. Milk cartons are in crates on a grate above this layer of milk. Milk is expired and the cooler smells of expired milk. Discussed with employees. Clean the interior of the cooler - wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 8/14/23. Ensure staff is aware to clean the base of the milk cooler when milk spills to prevent equipment being soiled.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed only one food handler’s license available in a folder. Multiple employees were in the kitchen during lunch hour and no copies of food handler’s licenses were available. Ensure copies of all employee’s food handler’s licenses are available for inspections. Ensure new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Discussed with PIC (arrived at end of inspection). Keep copies in the public health folder within the manager’s office. Correct by next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/14/23.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available during the inspection. Paperwork was in the filing cabinet at the dietary manager’s desk previously. Provided new copy of the agreement. Ensure all employees read and sign the document. Ensure all new hires read and sign the document as a part of onboarding. Keep in a public health folder/binder. Inspector will follow-up on 2/24/23.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed one employee working to be a CFPM; however, the other employee did not have a food handler’s licenses and/or a CFPM license. Employee stated she had a food handler’s card before, but it expired and she did not renew it. Ensure all employees have a valid food handler’s licenses (good for 3 years), unless the employee is a certified food protection manager. Ensure all new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival at the facility there was not a CFPM available. A CFPM (Rodney) arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Rodney is instructed to ensure that there are enough CFPM at the facility to cover all shifts moving foreword.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

1) Raw ground beef is observed on a tray in the standing cooler in the manager’s office mixed in with Ready-To-Eat (RTE) items. 2) Raw sausage is above RTE in the same cooler. Both items appear to be thawing and the PIC at the beginning of the inspection indicated that all the thawing foods area placed on the bottom shelf. A discussion took place with the PIC and the items were moved during the inspection to correct. TCS foods should be stored with the RTE items above all raw items in an cooler.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival, the PIC was not aware of where the reporting agreements for the food handlers were stored. A copy of the SCDPH reporting agreement was given to the PIC. They made copies and, because their full staff was here at the time of the inspection, had everyone sign one during th inspection to correct on site.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Three cans are observed on shelves in the dry storage area with major dents. PIC was consulted and the cans set aside for discard/ credit. PIC is aware that cans with major dents, or dents along the three seams should be set aside.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Black spots are observed in the ice in the ice machine. A single gnat was also observed on the ice in the ice machine. The ice was removed and the machine is scheduled to be cleaned later today.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

A spray bottle of disinfectant is observed stored on the shelf next to multiple metal strainers and containers. The container’s label does not have language indicating that it is safe for use on food contact surfaces. The container was moved to the chemical shelf during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The shelf under the dirty side of the dish machine is chipped/ rough. PIC instructed to repair so that it is maintained smooth and easily cleanable. 

(REPEAT x2) 1) The wall behind the dish machine is bubbled. Wall board is pulled away from the wall. 2) To left of the oven, the wall has a gap between two wall board sections. It also appears that this section of board is also pulling away from the wall the further to the left that you look. Repair/ seal to the wall.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At this time, there is not a CFPM at the facility. PIC is aware of the requirements and is attempting to get the company to purchase the training for those needing it in the kitchen.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Three cans are observed on shelves in the dry storage area with major dents. PIC was consulted and the cans set aside for discard/ credit. PIC is aware that cans with major dents, or dents along the three seams should be set aside.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, both buckets of sanitizer observed in the facility are observed low (0-100 ppm Quat). Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted.

1) Multiple probe thermometers and a measuring scoop are observed in cups that have soiled (sticky) bottoms. The cups also are used to store markers. Inspector discussed the situation with the PIC. The food contact surfaces should be stored in clean containers as well as in a way to prevent the potential contamination from other sources. The cups and thermometers were moved to cleaning to correct. 2) A metal drawer used to store cleaned utensils (to the left of the ovens) is heavily soiled. PIC moved the utensils and the drawer to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

A chipped section of flooring is accumulating debris under the shelves in the dry storage area. Repair so that the location is easily cleanable. 

(REPEAT) 1) The wall behind the dish machine is bubbled. Wall board is pulled away from the wall. 2) Caulk the handsink and sinks to the wall. 3) Seal base trim/coving around the handsink - look low. 4) To left of the oven, the wall has a gap between two wall board sections. 5) Under the same wall, the floor has 1/8" gap to wall that is collecting crumbs and debris. Seal the floor to the wall to eliminate the accumulation of food debris getting trapped in this gap. 6) Eliminate any holes in the wall - see around ovens. 7) Clean and paint the wall to the left of the ice machine.
